label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**TRANSPORTATION DEPARTMENT — WRITTEN STATEMENT**

**To:** Mrs. Okafor (parent of Amara Okafor, Kindergarten, Fairmont Elementary)
**From:** [Your Name], School Bus Driver — Bus 41, Route 9
**cc:** Darlene, Transportation Department
**Date:** [Insert date of submission]
**Re:** Statement regarding complaint dated October 29 — Tuesday, October 27, 2020 afternoon run, Kessler Ave. & Brandt St. stop (Bus 41, Route 9)

---

Mrs. Okafor,

I am writing this statement because a complaint was filed against me concerning the afternoon of Tuesday, October 27, and because you are receiving a copy of it. I want you to hear my account directly from me, in my own words, and I want it on record that I did what district policy requires of me. I do not expect you to agree with everything in here, and I am not writing to argue with you. I am writing to explain.

**What I did on October 27**

I was driving the afternoon run on Bus 41, Route 9, which serves Fairmont Elementary. One of my stops that afternoon was Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. Amara Okafor is a kindergartener on my route, and she rides with a green tag on her bag, which means an adult must be present at the stop to receive her. That is not a rule I set and it is not something I can decide to skip on a given day. It is the district's procedure for our kindergarten riders, and it is there because a five-year-old should never be standing at a corner alone.

We arrived at that stop at 3:52. The schedule time is 3:50. I waited at the corner until approximately 3:55, watching the area for a parent or guardian. I did not see anyone at the stop. I did not see a vehicle stopped on my side of the street with someone standing beside it, and I did not see anyone wave to me.

Because no adult was present and Amara had a green tag, the rule for kindergarten riders is that the student stays on the bus and is returned to the school, and the transportation office contacts the parent. So I kept Amara on the bus and continued on my route. At 3:56 I radioed dispatch, and Gloria at dispatch called Fairmont Elementary to let the school know Amara was coming back on the bus with me.

I had three more stops to run and 14 students still on board. I could not get off the bus and walk across the road or up to the corner to look for you. That is not something I am able to do with a full bus of children on it, and it is not something I would do even if the bus were empty, because I still have to keep the bus in view of every child on board. I want to be clear that this was not me choosing my convenience over your daughter. It was me choosing the safety of the 14 children I had with me and following the procedure for Amara.

We came back to Fairmont Elementary and I arrived at 4:31. I walked Amara into the office myself and turned her over to Mrs. Petrakis in the office. I did not leave her in the parking lot, in the office, or anywhere else on my own. There should be a record at the school of Amara being signed into the office at that time, and there should be a record of the 3:56 call from dispatch, and those records should match what I have written here.

**About you waving that afternoon**

You have told the school that you were parked across Brandt Street by the laundromat and that you waved to me. I believe you. I have no reason to doubt that you were there and that you waved, because you had every right to be there and every right to wave.

I did not see you. On that side of Brandt Street there was a box truck parked near the corner, and it blocked my view of the area where your car was. From the driver's seat of a bus, my sight line to the far side of that street was largely obscured by that truck. I was also looking at a five-year-old in the front of the bus, a kindergartener with a green tag who was standing up in the aisle and asking me why we were still at the stop. I want to be honest with you: my attention was on Amara, because she was on my bus and she needed an answer.

**About the report that I "drove off laughing"**

This was reported to the office, so I want to address it directly. I was not laughing. I was speaking to a fourth grader in seat 2, telling him to sit back down as we pulled out of the stop. When we pull away from a stop, some of the older students stand up and turn around in their seats, and I do not allow that while the bus is moving. I spoke to him in a normal, calm voice and told him to sit back down and face forward. That is the entire moment. Nobody on my bus was laughing, and I was certainly not laughing at you or at anything you did. I know how that must have looked from across the street, and I am sorry for it.

**How Amara was, and how I felt about all of this**

Amara was fine. She was not upset or frightened on the bus. She sat in her seat and colored on her folder, and at one point she asked me if she could ride the bus some more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip that day, which is what it was. I want you to know that I care about that child. She is a regular on my run and I look forward to seeing her.

I also want you to know that I understand why you were upset. You sent a five-year-old out to a street corner and she did not get on a bus and come home, and from where you were sitting she probably thought some stranger had taken her. If that had been one of my grandkids, I know exactly what that would have felt like, and I would have been just as alarmed as you were. I am sorry your daughter had a bad afternoon, and I am sorry you had a scary one. I am not sorry for following the rule that kept her from standing at a corner by herself, and I hope you can understand that those two things are both true at the same time.

**My request that the camera footage be pulled**

I am respectfully asking the Transportation Department to pull the interior and exterior camera footage from Bus 41 for the afternoon of October 27, covering the run from roughly 3:45 until the bus returned to Fairmont at 4:31. The camera should show the stop at Kessler and Brandt, how long we sat there, whether I got out of the bus (I did not), the students on board, and the fact that I stayed with Amara the entire time and walked her into the school office. I would also ask that the radio and dispatch log for that run be pulled, including the 3:56 call I made to Gloria.

I am not asking for this to prove that anybody is lying. I am asking for it because the record is more reliable than memory on both sides, and I would rather the file reflect what actually happened than what either of us thinks happened.

**What I am asking going forward**

I am glad to keep driving Amara. That is my sincere wish, and I hope we can put this behind us. But I would ask you — respectfully — to help me with the part that caused the problem. If you are able, please stand on the bus side of the street, on the corner where I can clearly see you, or step out of the car and wave from the curb. I know it is inconvenient, and I know the box truck was there and you had no way of knowing it would block my view, but from a bus I cannot always see across traffic, and I cannot get out and walk over to your car. If you are ever not able to make it to the curb, calling the school office or the transportation office before the run would also work, so we know you are there and waiting.

**In closing**

I have driven school buses in this district for 28 years, and I do not have a single write-up on my record. That is not me saying that I am perfect or that I cannot make a mistake, and I would not say anything like that to you. What I am saying is that I take this job seriously, I care about every child on my bus, and when a rule and a parent's expectation do not line up, I am going to follow the rule, because that rule is the reason children come home safe.

I am sorry for the worry and the fear that this caused you and your family. I would very much like for this to be resolved and for Amara and me to keep riding together. If you would like to talk about any of this, I am happy to do that in person or by phone, and I would rather talk with you than have something like this sitting between us.

Thank you for reading this. I appreciate you being a parent who came to the corner for her daughter every afternoon.

Respectfully,

[Your Name]
School Bus Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
Transportation Department
[Phone number]
[Signature]

---

A few things to check before you turn it in: your driver's name and signature, the date, and whether the district wants it on department letterhead or a specific form. Also, Darlene may want you to sign the original and note that a copy went to the parent — I'd confirm the submission process with her so there's a timestamp on it before the November 13 deadline.
